chapter: Gangsters, records, women musicians and the blues
title: Twelve years with the USO and thin dresses with Snub Mosley
summary: From World War II through Korea she was the only woman with Snub Mosley's 17 men, dressed in slinky dresses in the cold, and played stateside including Riker's Island.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Well, for 12 years I was with USO.
Yes. From the beginning of World War II to the end of the Korean War.
Whom did you work with that we might know?
Snub Mosely, I know, at one point.
Well, Snub Mosely was the last one. I was the only woman, though, with Snub Mosely.

With 17 men, because they said they didn't want no cry babies, and I had a lot of nerve. My bunk was (Unintelligible) -- near Russia, you know. And then Snub Mosely and all of them were working with their hats and their gloves and things on. That's the reason I've got this arthritis, I believe, because you see, I know men over there in those camps didn't want to see no woman come out there with no jeans and pants and things on, so I had -- well, I was supposed to look pretty decent, in a dress, so I had those slinky dresses, and I had nothing on but the dress, see?

Even in that cold weather. So they told me in later years I was going to feel it. Walter Winchell wrote a beautiful article and so did Dorothy Kilgallen, about me working in those thin dresses, and no coat or anything around me. And the men with their gloves and things on. And I didn't even catch cold. Never caught cold. But now I am. I'm suffering from it, you see, now. And then, after having gone through ETO and the South Pacific, then I did Stateside. I played all around here, all around the states, you know, all around, Chicago, Kansas City. Even played out here at Riker's Island.
